findings.reason: a node wiring the trigger must either be told that audit-class checks never set the retrieval flag or be given a probability for them, otherwise the reduce over flagged checks is undefined on exactly the class of check the section introduces.
findings.text: §2's done-when requires every check to hold a retrieval flag and permits a check to be decided by the audit finding class instead of a Jev question, so a flag-set audit-class check has no probability, and §5's trigger ("the maximum probability over the checks whose retrieval flag (§2) is set") then has a member with no defined input

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `review_names.md` resolves to `imas_codex/llm/prompts/sn/review_names.md`, `sn-house-style` §4 is "Conformance checks in the Layer 1 audits", and the `AuditReport` claim resolves at `imas_codex/standard_names/review/pipeline.py:1740`, where the report is turned into per-name findings.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §2's done-when is measurable (at least 80% of the 136 human edit reasons mapped) and declares a negative control (a test that fails when a check names an evidence field the review state does not carry).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §2 produces a taxonomy and a test rather than a gate log, and cites no scratchpad or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §2 carries no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag, and no changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2 requires a retrieval flag on every check while allowing a check to be decided by the `AuditReport` class with no Jev question, but §5 reduces the fanout trigger over the maximum probability of the flag-set checks, and an audit-class check carries no probability.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 carries one deliverable, the named-check taxonomy and its loader, with the keyword list and quorum deletion owned by §5 and §7.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §2 declares no cross-plan dependency and needs none (followup f-srtj-001 states it is the one section that needs no harness), and its consumers (§3 reads the taxonomy, §5 reduces over the flag) are named in prose.
